summary: Edward S. Casey is a philosopher who studied at Yale, Northwestern, and the Sorbonne under Paul Ricœur. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, Yale, and Stony Brook University, and served as president of the American Philosophical Association (2009–2010).

Edward Sapir was a linguist who studied at Columbia University under Franz Boas and Wilhelm Wundt. He served as Chief of Anthropology at the Geological Survey of Canada (ca. 1910–1925) and taught at the Universities of Chicago and Yale.
Edward Upham was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He was a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London and a member of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Edward Vernon Arnold was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Cambridge and the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He was a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge, and served as professor at Bangor University (1884–1924).
Edward W. Said studied at Princeton University and Harvard University. From around 1963 to 2003, he held an academic post in English and Comparative Literature at Columbia University.

Edward Washburn Hopkins was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, having also studied under Albrecht Weber. He taught at Columbia, Bryn Mawr, and Yale (1895–1926), also editing the Journal of the American Oriental Society.

Edward Winslow Bastian is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, while also training under other traditional Tibetan teachers.

Edwin Arnold was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Oxford. He served as principal of Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and later taught as a visiting lecturer at Keio University.

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson, educated at Trinity College Dublin, worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (ca. 1880–1890) and was President of The Asiatic Society (1886–1887).

Edwin Francis Bryant is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at Columbia University, taught at Harvard University (ca. 1997–2000), and became an Associate Professor of Hinduism at Rutgers University around 2003.

Edwin Gerow was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Louis Renou, among others. He held faculty posts at the University of Washington and Reed College (1978–1998) and edited JAOS.

Edwin Norris was a scholar of linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a translator for the Foreign Office and held positions including assistant secretary, librarian, and honorary secretary at the Royal Asiatic Society between 1836 and 1872.

Edwin Whitfield Fay was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield and Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve. He was a professor at Washington and Lee University and the University of Texas at Austin.

Egaku Maeda was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctorate at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, and Hajime Nakamura. He served as a professor at Meijo University and Aichi Gakuin University (1972–2002).

Eido Shimano was a Buddhist studies and religious figure who studied under Kengan Goto and Soen Nakagawa. He served as abbot of the Zen Studies Society and as shike at New York Zendo Shobo-ji and Dai Bosatsu Zendo Kongo-ji.

Eiichi Imoto was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He served on the faculty at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (ca. 1964–1993) and Momoyama Gakuin University (ca. 1993–2001).

Eiichi Makino was a scholar of philosophy and law who studied at the University of Tokyo. He subsequently taught at the University of Tokyo (ca. 1903–1938), Shiraume Gakuen Junior College (ca. 1953–1968), and several other Japanese universities.

Eiichi Otani is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed his education at Toyo University around 1987 to 1991. As of 2026, he is attested as dean and professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University.
Eiichi Yamaguchi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed graduate studies at Kyushu University between 1986 and 1990 and served as a research assistant there around 1990–1991.
Eiju Fukushima is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history and archaeology. As of 2026, he is attested as a faculty member at Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.
